guide.lumaReadsExistingMediaInDirectoriesMount:
Your library starts with a folder on the Luma server, with its subfolders shown as albums. In Docker, mount your media folder and use the path inside the container when configuring it.

For another disk or network share, add a mount and library entry, then restart Luma.
guide.stableLibraryIDsAndIndexing: Add a library and start browsing
guide.useConsecutiveConfigurationIndexesStarti:
Number your configuration entries from 0 without gaps, and give each library a unique ID. Keep those IDs when upgrading so Luma can recognize your existing libraries.

On your first visit, choose whether to scan the whole library or discover folders as you open them. Read-only access is fine for browsing, tagging, playback and captions.
guide.dockerEnvironmentThenSettingsGeneralFile: Docker environment, then Settings → General → File management
guide.turnOnEnableFileManagementInSettingsGene:
To upload or change files, turn on Enable file management in Settings → General → File management. Give each library you want to edit Writable=true and a :rw media mount.

Your choice applies across devices. For a fresh installation, you can set the default with Luma__Files__Enabled; after that, the saved setting takes priority.
guide.startupBannerSettingsGeneralFileManageme: Startup banner / Settings → General → File management
guide.lumaChecksWriteAccessAtStartupAndWhenEna:
Seeing a read-only notice? Check your library’s mount and permissions, then choose Check media mounts in Settings to try again. You’ll see the result for each library.

You can still browse and tag read-only media. Dismiss the notice if that’s all you need; it won’t appear again until the server restarts.
guide.theEmptyStartPageHasAddComicLocationIt:
Start with Add comic location in Panels, or open Comic locations to add to an existing bookshelf. Pick a library and browse to your comic folder; leaving the path empty includes the entire library. Folder search covers indexed folders, but you can browse unindexed ones too.

Choose Save locations and scan when you’re ready. For comics stored as loose images, tick Treat folders containing images as comics. You can follow discovery in Background jobs, and read-only libraries work here too.
guide.checkedByDefaultForEachComicLocationIncl:
Keep comic pages out of your photo collection with Exclude from Gallery, which is on by default. This also leaves them out of Gallery’s tag collections and XMP exports without losing tags or reading progress.

To include them again, untick the option and rescan for any new files. Check parent comic locations too: an excluded parent hides its subfolders. Folders you’ve hidden manually need to be shown separately.

For new installations, set Luma__Panels__Sources__0__ExcludeFromGallery to choose the default. Saved locations take priority, and separate server libraries need non-overlapping roots.
guide.thePanelsStartPageShowsUpToFiveRecently:
Pick up one of your five most recent unfinished comics from Continue reading, or explore your saved folders below. Use Up to go back a folder and Bookshelf to return to your locations.

Find a book by title, author or series, or narrow the list by reading status, favourites or comic tags. Searching from the bookshelf covers all locations; inside a library, it covers that library. Add tags through Details — tags used only for comics won’t clutter Gallery.

You can reorganize your locations anytime in Comic locations. Removing one keeps the books’ details and your reading progress for later.
guide.galleryIsAlwaysAvailableEnableOrHideFlic:
Make Luma suit your collection in Settings → General → Applications. Flick and Panels start enabled, and you can turn either off across all your devices.

For a fresh server, set Luma__Ui__FlickEnabled and Luma__Ui__PanelsEnabled to choose the defaults. Once you’ve saved a choice in Settings, that takes priority.
guide.backUpSQLiteAndOriginalStagingTrashMedia: Before upgrading, stop Luma and back up the database together with your media, staging and trash folders. To roll back, restore that matching backup and the older Luma image.
guide.switchApplicationsManageWritableLibrarie: Apps, file management, uploads and recovery
guide.clickTheLumaLogoToChooseGalleryFlickOr: In the mood for photos, videos or a comic? Choose Gallery, Flick or Panels from the Luma logo. The icon beside it shows where you are, and each app remembers its own search and filters.
guide.searchComicTitlesOrSeriesFilterBySeriesC:
Open a comic to pick up where you left off. For a different title, cover or other book details, use Details on the bookshelf.

Make reading comfortable in Reader settings: choose a page layout, reading direction, fit and zoom, or go fullscreen. Pinch to zoom, drag to pan, and tap the page counter to jump ahead. You can also turn pages with swipes, arrow buttons or keyboard shortcuts.

Your place is saved as you read. When you’re done, Exit reader takes you back to the shelf.
guide.galleryInsideAConfiguredWritableLibrary: Gallery, inside a configured writable library
guide.useTheFileManagementIconBesideSelectToRe:
Open file management beside Select, then choose the files or folders you’d like to work with. To move or copy them, choose Cut or Copy, browse to another folder in the same library and Paste. You can rename one selected item, or create folders and upload into the folder you’re viewing.

If a name is already taken, choose Replace or Skip. You can use the same choice for the rest of the batch. Replacing a folder sends the entire old folder to the recycle bin rather than merging its contents.

Delete uses the recycle bin unless you choose permanent deletion. You’ll also find Delete in the Gallery viewer and Flick menus, and Rename in the Gallery viewer. File management is available in search and tag results too.

Follow your tasks in Background jobs. With file management open, Ctrl/Cmd+X, C, V and Delete work outside text fields and dialogs. Copied items stay on the clipboard for another paste; cut items clear once the move is queued.
guide.theUploadDialogHasChooseFilesChooseFolde:
Drop files or folders into the upload window, or use the file and folder pickers. Your folder structure comes with them. Feel free to close the window and browse while uploading; progress is in Background jobs.

If you refresh the page, choose the same files to pick up where you left off. For names already in use, you’ll be asked whether to replace or skip.

guide.chooseAWritableLibraryShowsOriginalPaths:
Accidentally deleted something? Pick its library in the recycle bin and choose Restore to put it back. If the old path is already taken, enter another path in the same library. Restoring needs write access.

Recycled files still use disk space until you delete them permanently. The recycle bin is useful for undoing mistakes, but keep a separate backup too.

guide.forMovieMkvOrMovieMp4PlaceMovieSrt:
Put movie.srt beside movie.mkv or movie.mp4. Uppercase .SRT works too. Language suffixes such as movie.en.srt and files in other folders aren’t matched.

Embedded tracks must use SubRip/SRT. ASS/SSA, PGS/VobSub and MP4 mov_text aren’t supported. Use UTF-8 or BOM-marked UTF-16 text, up to 4 MiB. Luma doesn’t generate subtitles or read them from images.
guide.stylizedSubtitlesAreNotSupportedAuthorFo:
Captions use plain text, without custom fonts, colors, positioning or effects. Temporary and converted subtitle files are kept in Luma’s cache, away from your originals.

If captions fail to load, turn CC off and on to try again.

guide.deploymentPreferenceKeys:
Set a deployment default with Luma__Ui__Preferences__ followed by the preference key. Use string values and quoted objects for JSON settings. Saved choices in the app take priority.

Supported keys: luma-theme, luma-appearance-v2, luma-album-covers, luma-reels-sort, luma-slideshow-seconds, luma-video-autoplay, luma-viewer-fill, luma-reels-fill, luma-show-filters, luma-reels-show-filters, luma-reels-state, luma-panels-reader-defaults.

Boolean settings accept true/false or 1/0; inside JSON, use true or false. Reader defaults apply to comics without saved preferences.
